title: Kalman filters: dynamic hedge ratios
dek: Building a Kalman filter from scratch in NumPy to track a drifting hedge ratio — and an honest accounting of what adaptivity buys after costs.
excerpt: Static hedge ratios assume the relationship never moves; on EWA/EWC 2010–2024 it moves from 0.71 to 1.49. We treat beta as a random-walk state, filter it in five lines of NumPy, and trade the spread both ways — the Kalman beta wins as an estimator (gross Sharpe 0.55 vs 0.47, half the drawdown), while 10 bp costs on 2.7× turnover decide the net line.
